clinician.trajectory_summary: The patient, a renal transplant recipient on chronic immunosuppression (prednisone 20 mg/day and mycophenolate 5.760 mg/day for 15 years), presented with a one-year history of bilateral painful subcutaneous nodules (2 cm, firm, adherent, erythematous/cyanotic skin) on the right arm and left forearm, accompanied by systemic symptoms (fever, cough, weight loss) that began simultaneously with the nodules. Initial evaluation revealed a TB-suggestive pulmonary image despite negative sputum AFB cultures, leading to empiric anti-tuberculosis therapy that persisted for one year. One year after symptom onset, biopsy of the right arm nodule demonstrated macrophage proliferation, multinucleated giant cells, and lymphoplasmacytic neutrophilic infiltrate with abundant intracytoplasmatic microorganisms characteristic of H. capsulatum on methenamine silver staining, confirming the diagnosis of disseminated histoplasmosis involving the skin/subcutaneous tissue and lungs.
